solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: After theatre in Broadway, Mary Jane was perfect

parts.note: beyond, as in 'beyond the hill', means further on or after
rep is short for repertory theatre
Mary Jane is slang for marijuana, and a roach is the butt of a cannabis joint

explanation.surface: A Broadway actress named Mary Jane gave a flawless performance after the show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Broadway' just sets the scene for the theatre; the pieces are simply strung together.
explanation.definitionFit: Something above any criticism is faultless, which is what perfect means.

clue.text: Support chair to club vexatious passenger

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
a chair is a seat
a driver is a golf club used for long tee shots

explanation.surface: Someone props up a chair to hit an irritating passenger with a club.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for a car passenger who keeps giving the driver unwanted instructions, which is vexing.

clue.text: Does its consumption make one cultured?

definitions.text: Does its consumption make one cultured?

parts.words: Does its consumption make one cultured?
parts.note: cultured seems to mean refined, but this food is made with bacterial cultures, so eating it fills one with cultures

explanation.surface: A wry question whether eating something can make a person sophisticated.
explanation.definitionFit: This milk product is fermented with live bacterial cultures, a variant spelling of the more usual form.

parts.note: to need something is to demand or require it
less means a smaller amount

explanation.surface: A request for less of something is pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: A thing not needed at all is superfluous, or unnecessary.

clue.text: Red bible did not begin to be fit for consumption

indicators.note: each of the two words loses its opening letter, so neither begins as printed

explanation.surface: A red Bible failed to start being something one could eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Food safe to eat is fit for consumption.

clue.text: Turn Dad's Army into repetitive performance

indicators.note: the army goes into the performance, splitting it open

parts.note: rote is mechanical repetition, as in learning by rote
TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's part-time volunteer reserve, here likened to the Home Guard of the TV sitcom Dad's Army

explanation.surface: The sitcom Dad's Army gets turned into a show done over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: Dad's Army is a British TV comedy about the wartime Home Guard of older volunteers; the clue uses it for the part-time TA.
explanation.definitionFit: To spin round an axis is to turn, a direct synonym.

definitions.meaning: a fight in war, as in killed in ...

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both combat with the enemy and a notable deed someone performs.

clue.text: Remedial niche created around Britain for planted remedy

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the abbreviation for Britain
the letters are created afresh into a new arrangement

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for Britain (as on car plates, GB)

explanation.surface: A healing nook built around Britain to supply plant-based cures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'created' rearranges REMEDIAL NICHE to HERALMEDICINE, and 'around' wraps those letters round B.
explanation.definitionFit: Treatment made from plants is a remedy that is, playfully, planted.

parts.note: in the Andersen tale the ugly duckling is really a young swan

explanation.definitionFit: The fairy-tale bird mocked as an ugly duckling grows into a swan, so it was a baby swan all along.

clue.text: Hitler was a great film for Chaplin

definitions.text: Hitler was a great film for Chaplin

parts.words: Hitler was a great film for Chaplin
parts.note: Hitler was an autocrat, and Chaplin's 1940 satire of him was titled The Great one of these

explanation.surface: A remark that Hitler made fine film material for Charlie Chaplin.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitler was an absolute ruler, a tyrant, and Chaplin's film The Great ___ lampooned him.

clue.text: The Italian in trouble is injured

indicators.note: the Italian word goes inside the word for trouble

parts.note: a spot of trouble, as in in a tight spot
il is the Italian for the

explanation.surface: An Italian man in difficulty has been hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Something damaged or impaired has been harmed, so injured fits loosely.

indicators.note: a meltdown breaks things down so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An excess of water comes from melting polar ice.
explanation.definitionFit: A glut or excess is a superabundance.

definitions.meaning: to keep company with, team up with

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means teaming up with someone; as a noun it is an associate or ally.

clue.text: More of Miss West in Scotland

definitions.meaning: in Scots dialect the word for more
the American actress West, of 'Come up and see me sometime'

explanation.surface: Asking for more films of Mae West to be shown in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Scotland' tells you the first sense is Scots dialect.
explanation.definitionFit: Scots uses this word for more, and it is the first name of the film star West.

clue.text: This clue of a religious symbol

parts.note: the cross is the symbol of Christianity

explanation.surface: A clue made from a religious emblem.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition refers to the clue's own place in the grid: it is an across entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue sits in the horizontal list of the grid, so it describes itself.

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: feeling out of sorts is feeling unwell or ill

explanation.surface: Feeling more or less unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for thus, inserted in quotations to show an error is the original's, so it means so.

indicators.note: principally means chiefly, pointing to the principal, first letters of each word

explanation.surface: A statement that the main English habit is this drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The English are famously hooked on this hot drink, and its letters open the three words.

clue.text: The Age of Aquarius for wanton sex, is it?

indicators.note: wanton means unrestrained or wild, so the letters run riot

explanation.surface: Asking whether the hippy era was about free love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Age of Aquarius' is the hippy song from the musical Hair, standing for that decade of free love.
explanation.definitionFit: The Age of Aquarius, from the musical Hair, is the anthem of that hippie decade.

clue.text: He walks with a baby carriage

definitions.meaning: a pushchair, the usual American term for a pram

explanation.surface: A man walks along pushing a pram.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a leisurely walker and a pushchair for a baby.

clue.text: Malaysian national symbol is in his club, left out and devastated

indicators.note: devastated means wrecked, so the letters are broken up
out tells us the letter for left is removed from the words his club

explanation.surface: A Malaysian emblem is at his club, but he has been left out and is heartbroken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes L from HIS CLUB, leaving HISCUB; 'devastated' then rearranges IS plus HISCUB.
explanation.definitionFit: This red flower, the bunga raya, is the national flower of Malaysia.

parts.note: an gives the indefinite article A
TT, teetotal, describes someone who abstains from alcohol
ire is anger, a passion

explanation.surface: Clothe a teetotaller with fervour.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing worn, a synonym for dress as a noun or verb.

clue.text: A quiet look to the doctor for assurance

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
lo, as in lo and behold, means look
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A discreet glance at the physician for reassurance.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-assured poise and composure is assurance.

parts.note: ave is Latin hail, a greeting
RN, the Royal Navy, are sailors

explanation.surface: A time to call out to a group of sailors.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'local' is British for one's neighbourhood pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A local is the nearby pub, and a tavern is an inn or pub.

definitions.meaning: short for veteran, one long experienced
to check thoroughly, as in vetting a candidate

explanation.definitionFit: Three meanings: a seasoned veteran, a veterinarian, and to examine closely.

indicators.note: the letters are taken from within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Some sort of fastener found at a railway level crossing.
explanation.definitionFit: A hook-and-loop fastening fabric, sold under a trade name.

definitions.meaning: a gun that fires several shots without reloading
one who offends again and again

explanation.definitionFit: Both a gun firing repeatedly and a criminal who reoffends again and again.

definitions.note: two slash marks, each a diagonal stroke

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the following words

explanation.surface: Two slashes in front of a remark about dropping a parasol.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the typographical symbol itself: two forward slashes.
explanation.definitionFit: A forward slash is called a solidus in typography, and two of them are its Latin plural.

clue.text: Cable television dishing out bestial programme of brutality

indicators.note: the letters of the word bestial are dished out, taken away from the pool
programme means arrange, so what is left is sorted into a new order

explanation.surface: Cable TV is airing a beastly show full of savagery.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the letters of BESTIAL from CABLE TELEVISION ('dishing out') and 'programme' rearranges the remaining CLEEVION.
explanation.definitionFit: Brutality is savage, cruel force, which is a synonym.

indicators.note: the words hug the answer between them, holding it inside

explanation.surface: Felt-made toys hugged by the children of an envoy.
explanation.definitionFit: A Turkish word for an ambassador or envoy, used in English.

parts.note: Friday seems a day of the week but is Man Friday, servant of the castaway in Defoe's novel

explanation.surface: Someone to spend Friday with.
explanation.definitionFit: In Defoe's novel the castaway's companion is Man Friday, so he is Friday's companion.
